answer: An island freight co-op serving vine growers and marble cutters could require each voting ID to burn 2 tokens and deliver one assigned pallet per epoch. Dock inspectors sign ID/epoch-bound dispatch and arrival receipts with a unique seal number. Validators check the ID-bound burn and both signatures, rejecting reused burns or seals. n IDs burn 2n tokens and owe n deliveries. Failed checks or missed arrivals deny that epoch's vote without refund. Colluding inspectors can fake freight; efficient fleets cut labor costs, and wealth still buys votes.
